newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 16.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- China reports victory in Geneva an anti-China attempt by group of Western countries, led by United States, at session of United Nations Commission on Human Rights.
- Front-page commentary hails China's success in defeating anti-China attempt on human rights.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH

- Foreign Ministry spokesman says China will postpone planned exchange of visits with Denmark and freeze exchanges and cooperation in human rights area because it took lead in putting forth anti-China motion at U.N. Human Rights Commission
- Visiting Russian Minister of National Defence Igor Rodionov says Sino-Russian partnership of strategic cooperation will facilitate establishment of new, fair and multipolar world order
- Chinese president Jiang Zemin speaks highly of Sino-Mauritian relations in meeting with visiting Mauritian Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam.
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- Shanghai auto industry to sell 60,000 Santana cars to taxi sector
- Regions slightly raise coal prices
- Vietnamese traders rush to buy potatoes, onoins after border area hit by disasters
MARKET DAILY
- Jiangsu province attracts $9.6 billion in Taiwan investment at end third quarter of 1996
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- Yellow River flow at its lowest level, experts warn of water shortages
- State Land Adminstration issues circular to ban rampant use of farmland
CHINA DAILY
- China will start nationwide inspection of 70,000 small factories ordered to shut down by State Council for seriously polluting environment
- Seven Chinese businessmen sentenced to imprisonment for pirating video and audio compact disks.
